extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators and institutional research administrators preparing pre-applications and full applications for the DOE Office of Science Early Career Research Program (FY2024)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing and submitting pre-applications and full applications to the DOE Office of Science Early Career Research Program (FY2024), including eligibility, budget rules, pre-application screening criteria, required attachments, reviewer scoring, and award/selection considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application review criteria — Responsiveness to FOA objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsiveness to the objectives of the FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-applications will be reviewed for responsiveness of the proposed work to the research topics identified in the funding announcement. Program Managers may move pre-applications between topical areas and will issue an encourage/discourage decision based on topical fit. Only those pre-applications judged responsive and encouraged may submit a full application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application review criteria — Scientific and technical merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific and technical merit (one of the factors used by Program Managers when evaluating pre-applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal Program Managers evaluate pre-applications for scientific and technical merit and, when a topical area is oversubscribed, may comparatively evaluate competitiveness within the topic to encourage or discourage submission of full applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application review criteria — Appropriateness of research approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of the proposed research approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Managers will assess whether the proposed research approaches are appropriate to accomplish the stated objectives and fit within the topical area described in the FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application review criteria — Likelihood of scientific impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Likelihood of scientific impact of the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-application comparative reviews give priority to scientifically innovative and forward-looking basic research with the highest likelihood of success as a full application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application review criteria — Ensuring a diverse pool of applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of ensuring a diverse pool of applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Managers may consider how a pre-application contributes to a diverse applicant pool when encouraging or discouraging full application submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review criteria (general) — Seven criteria and narrative comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be evaluated against seven merit review criteria (applicants and reviewers should consult the FOA for the full list).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers provide narrative comments associated with each of the seven merit review criteria; applicants should prepare their applications to address all criteria per the FOA. The solicitation contains the full descriptions of the seven criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review criterion 7 — Potential for Leadership within the Scientific Community
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion 7: Potential for leadership within the scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers interpret scientific leadership broadly by discipline. The Office of Science is looking for researchers early in their careers who can develop new scientific ideas, promote them, and convince peers to pursue them. Appendix 1 should include information to evaluate leadership (examples: invited/public lectures, awards, program committees, conference/workshop organization, professional society activities, international/industrial partnerships, reviewing/editorship activities). Reviewers should apply professional judgment of what leadership means in the discipline. This criterion is also used to help select nominees for PECASE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer overall numerical rating scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reviewer provides an overall integer numerical rating between 1 and 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale categories: Strongly Encourage Funding (5 or 6); Encourage Funding (3 or 4); Discourage Funding (1 or 2). Reviewers also provide narrative comments for each merit review criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection official considerations and program policy factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection Official considers merit review scores and written recommendations plus program policy factors and available funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program policy factors may include relevance to Office of Science priorities, promoting diversity of supported investigators and institutions, and increasing participation of institutions historically underrepresented in the SC research portfolio. A full list of program policy factors appears in the FOA (page 90).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Definition of 'early career' and Ph.D. window
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators are within 12 years of having received a Ph.D. for FY2024 (doctoral conferment on or after January 1, 2011).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SC intends to revert to a 10-year window in later competitions. Extensions to the eligibility window will be considered for individuals with a major life event requiring an extended absence (three months or longer). PIs must have a Ph.D. by the application due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Eligible PI employment categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible PIs: untenured assistant professors on the tenure track, untenured associate professors on the tenure track, or full-time, non-postdoctoral, permanent employees at a DOE national laboratory or an SC Scientific User Facility not at a DOE national laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PI must be employed by a U.S. academic institution, a DOE national laboratory, or an SC Scientific User Facility. For university-based PIs, the PI must be in the tenure-track position as of the application due date. Employment and appointment details must be true as of the application due date shown on the FOA cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility extensions for major life events
rubrics_metrics.description: Process for requesting an extension to eligibility due to a major life event (extended absence >= three months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a letter signed by the dean, research vice president, or equivalent official stating the proposed PI will have, as of the application deadline, no more than 12 years of full-time professional work experience in positions requiring a Ph.D. The letter must include NO personal information about the reason for the absence. The request is evaluated as part of the pre-application assessment and determinations do not carry over between years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment-type eligibility test for national laboratory / user-facility staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Five-question test program for lab/User Facility appointment types to determine eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions: (1) Is the appointment type considered postdoctoral? (2) Is an appointee an employee of the lab or user facility? (3) Is the institution's intention to transition appointees to career employment? (4) Is the appointment full time? (5) Does the appointment qualify for full benefits of a career employee? If Q1 = no and Q2–Q5 = yes, the appointment type is eligible. DOE maintains lists of previously approved/disapproved position types; institutions should clear ambiguous appointment types with DOE.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI participation limit and what counts as participation
rubrics_metrics.description: A Principal Investigator may not participate in more than three Office of Science ECRP competitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation is defined as submission of a full application that has not been withdrawn before being officially declined or that was not declined without merit review. Submission of a pre-application does NOT count as participation. Withdrawn applications prior to official decline (subject to rules described) may not count; consult FOA and PAMS status rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-PI requirement and prohibition on co-Principal Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a single-Principal Investigator program; co-PIs are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications including co-PIs may be declined without review. Multiple early career investigators should not propose a single large award with multiple PIs. Paid collaborators are discouraged unless they bring something unique; collaboration can be described and supported but should not substitute for a PI-led project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget minimums, salary expectations, and indirects
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum award size: approximately $875,000 for five years for universities; approximately $2,750,000 for five years for DOE national laboratories or SC User Facilities. Minimums include direct and indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical lab awards historically $500k/year are being raised to ~$550k/year. Laboratory/SC User Facility awards are encouraged to cover at least 50% of PI salary; if less than 50% it should be as close to 50% as possible. Requests larger than historical averages are possible with appropriate justification. No cost sharing is required. The cumulative budget may be distributed across years as desired, but labs are strongly encouraged to charge ~50% PI salary each year. PAMS allows a maximum of five budget periods entered in one-year increments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation prohibited; letters of collaboration allowed (strict format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of recommendation, endorsement, or support are not allowed. Optional letters of collaboration may be included but must conform to a strict two-sentence format and be placed in Appendix 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each optional letter of collaboration may contain two and only two sentences and must follow a provided template starting 'Dear <Principal Investigator Name>:' and stating intent to collaborate with one very short description sentence. Applications that include recommendation letters will be subject to elimination during DOE’s initial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management plan required
rubrics_metrics.description: A data management plan (DMP) is required and must be included in Appendix 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the solicitation for guidance and to the DOE Office of Science Statement on Digital Data Management. The DOE Office of Science will decline without review any application that does not include a data management plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting Inclusive and Equitable Research (PIER) plan required
rubrics_metrics.description: A PIER plan must be included in Appendix 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the solicitation for guidance on the PIER plan and to SC website resources. The PIER plan is a required attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synergistic activities / biographical sketch content for leadership evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of synergistic activities is required in the biographical sketch to help evaluate potential for leadership (criterion 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include professional and scholarly activities related to the proposed effort that demonstrate leadership potential: invited/public lectures, awards, program committees, conference organization, society activities, partnerships, reviewing/editorships, etc. Use Appendix 1 as instructed in the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application format, length, and submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-application is required, limited to three pages, and must be submitted via PAMS by an authorized institutional representative (institutional countersignature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no separate cover page — the header information should fit within the three pages. Figures and citations may be included but everything must fit within the three pages and use at least 11-point font. Pre-applications are reviewed for responsiveness and competitiveness; historically ~80% were encouraged but this may change with oversubscription. Only encouraged pre-applications may submit full applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full application format, page limits, and submission route
rubrics_metrics.description: Full applications must conform to the FOA requirements and be submitted electronically through Grants.gov (FOA DE-FOA-0003176).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first-page header information may be placed on a separate cover page outside the 15-page narrative. A table of contents is allowed and does not count toward the 15-page limit. National Laboratories must submit through Grants.gov and cannot submit the full proposal directly in PAMS. Field Work Proposals (FWP) should not be submitted at this time; FWP may be requested later for those selected for possible funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on changes and corrections after deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes after deadlines are not allowed; corrections before the deadline require resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may correct typos before the deadline by submitting the application again via Grants.gov, checking the 'Changed/Corrected Application' box, and emailing SC.Early@science.doe.gov. Changes after the deadline are not allowed. Omitted required attachments (e.g., DMP) will lead to decline without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process modalities and reviewer feedback availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be reviewed by mail review, panel review, or a combination; reviewers provide narrative comments and an overall integer rating; reviewer comments are accessible to PIs after funding recommendation or decline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each program office decides its review method. Applicants should follow the FOA review criteria and format to prepare. Reviewer comments will be available in PAMS at the time or shortly after the application is recommended for funding or declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested 'do not involve' reviewers protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may suggest reviewers not to involve, but this should be sent to the program manager by email rather than included in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify your pre-application title and institution in the email. Do not include lists of reviewers to avoid in the application or pre-application because these documents will be seen by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on duplication of currently funded research and concurrent funding policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The application may not duplicate research for which the PI is already funded; concurrent submissions to other agencies are allowed but acceptance rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may submit the same proposal to two federal agencies (e.g., DOE and NSF), but you cannot be funded twice by the federal government for the same scope of work. If both agencies select the proposal, you may accept only one award for the duplicated scope; to accept both, propose distinct scopes of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical area selection and constraints after encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a single topical area for pre-application submission; if encouraged by a program office, the full application must be submitted to that office and cannot be moved afterward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your idea cuts across topical areas, choose the primary topical area. Program Managers may reassign pre-applications before encouragement. Once a pre-application is encouraged by a particular program office, the associated application must be reviewed within that program office and must meet any office-specific data management requirements described in the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAMS submission and account registration rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-applications must be submitted directly into PAMS; PAMS is integrated with Grants.gov for full application import.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register in PAMS by creating an individual account then associating with your institution. Pre-apps in PAMS must be submitted by a user with 'Submit to DOE' privilege (institutional countersignature). For technical difficulties with PAMS before the deadline, contact the PAMS help desk and, if necessary, SC.Early@science.doe.gov with details and help-desk tracking number for consideration of late submission.
